shill: rtnl: Overload SendMessage to transfer RTNLMessage ownership RTNLHandler::SendMessage currently does not allow for RTNLMessage ownership to be transfered from the client to RTNLHandler. This prevents RTNLHandler from having context of a particular RTNLMessage when the corresponding RTNL response is received (without copying the RTNLMessage, that is). This change provides an overload for SendMessage that does allow for this. This implementation is careful to only allow a certain window of sequences to be stored at any given time. If a particular request happens not to get a response (for whatever reason), this would essentially leak the memory of that RTNLMessage. LOG-ing when this occurs will allow us to determine why this occurred. When clients use this SendMessage overload, if the message results in an RTNL error, RTNLHandler will provide a clear an informative error log. BUG=chromium:958674 TEST=-All unit tests are passing. Change-Id: I41ded8d621e0b4930f922148bfee740388e072b7 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1594974 Commit-Ready: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Tested-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org>

shill: routing: Transfer RTNLMessage ownership to RTNLHandler RTNLHandler is switching from a SendMessage interface that takes a raw RTNLMessage pointer to one that takes a unique_ptr<RTNLMessage>, such that clients can transfer RTNLMessage ownership to RTNLHandler. The relevant changes are made to RoutingTable to use this new interface. Now RTNL errors caused by RoutingTable code will provide an informative error message, like that shown in the TEST section. BUG=chromium:958674 TEST=-All unit tests are passing. -Manually tested to generate an RTNL routing error. Saw error message like: "sequence 187 (Delete Route: RouteStatus dst_prefix 8 src_prefix 0 table 255 protocol 3 scope 0 type 1 flags 0) recevied error 3 (No such process)" Rather than the usual: "sequence 187 received error 3 (No such process)". common/usb_pd_protocol: Avoid unitialized use of port flags On reset, when pd_partner_port_reset is called, if, for any reason pd_get_saved_port_flags fails to get the saved port status, we would risk using unitialized flags from the stack. The function logic was a little complicated, and can be simplified quite a bit by returning early if no contract is in place (or if we fail to read flags from BBRAM). This should not be a problem on real boards, as the stored value should be readable from BBRAM. In any case, the first time we used the flag if (explicit_contract_in_place && pd_comm_is_enabled(port)) only applies to unlocked RO images, so this never happens in production (where RO images are locked). The second case is a little tricker, and we may end up (not) applying Rp where we should (not): /* If we just lost power, don't apply Rp. */ if (!explicit_contract_in_place || system_get_reset_flags() & (RESET_FLAG_BROWNOUT | RESET_FLAG_POWER_ON)) return; Presumably, the worst case here is that a charger may not work after a brownout/power on. BRANCH=none BUG=chromium:958510 TEST=setup_board --board=amd64-generic --profile=msan-fuzzer cros_fuzz --board=amd64-generic reproduce --fuzzer \ chromeos_ec_usb_pd_fuzzer --testcase \ ./clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ec_usb_pd_fuzzer-5086219896225792 \ --package chromeos-ec --build-type msan => No more MemorySanitizer error. init: Only keep at most 21 recent logs when cleaning logs There are cases when we may have a lot of log files in a directory even though none of them are more than a week old and all of them are small. One synthetic test that shows this are reboot tests where we do reboot after reboot in a short period of time. ...but you could also imagine a crashing or misbehaving process could also do something similar. At the moment all these files slow down boot quite a bit (see chromium:961127). Presumably we should fix that so boot isn't slowed down by lots of files, but it's probably also wise to trim the directories down a bit. NOTE: We only actually run log rotation once per day, so the number of logs can still get quite big. At least this should trim it down a little, though. BUG=chromium:961107 TEST=Boot and there are lots fewer log files now Change-Id: I9e4f707a050da201a1cd7175f96ea5d06fa9501e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1605602 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Tested-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

ish/ish5: fixed both-edge triggered gpio configuration blocking D0ix issue ISH PMU does not support both-edge interrupt triggered gpio configuration. If both edges are configured, then the ISH can't stay in low power mode because it will exit immediately. As a W/A, we scan all gpio pins which have been configured as both-edge triggered, and then temporarily set each gpio pin to the single edge trigger that is opposite of its value, then restore the both-edge trigger configuration immediately after exiting low power mode. site_linux_router: truncate (not delete) uma-events We're removing this file, but that can confuse other daemons, which may then accidentally re-create the file with different owners/permissions, locking out non-root daemons. Rather than tease out the expected permissions or force all system daemons to configure the correct owners/permissions, let's just avoid deleting the file -- we can truncate it instead, which will retain its original permissions. Noticed in b:131906820, where shill is repeatedly complaining: ERR shill[646]: [ERROR:serialization_utils.cc(290)] /var/lib/metrics/uma-events: cannot open: Permission denied BUG=none TEST=run network_WiFi_* test; watch size, permissions of .../uma-events Change-Id: I8096917d385bab44444c8252acf702eab7a18407 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1600456 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Harpreet Grewal <harpreet@chromium.org>
